purpose: personal account of the market analysis of AI Engineer job descriptions

required_facts.fact: The analysis covered more than 1,000 AI Engineer job descriptions from Berlin, Amsterdam, London, Los Angeles, and New York.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 3: sample size and locations are stated.

required_facts.fact: An LLM classified 889 descriptions into AI-first, AI-support, and traditional ML/DL categories.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 6: classification method and count are specified.

required_facts.fact: AI-first roles were about 70 percent and involved LLM or GenAI systems, RAG, agents, evaluation, and production deployment.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 8: category share and work are described.

required_facts.fact: AI-support roles were about 28.5 percent and focused on platforms, GPU/inference infrastructure, pipelines, deployment, monitoring, or experimentation interfaces.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 9: support category and responsibilities are listed.

required_facts.fact: Traditional ML/DL roles were fewer than 2 percent and resembled ML Engineer or Research Engineer work.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 10: category size and character are stated.

required_facts.fact: The proposed market definition centered on owning design, evaluation, and production operation of foundation-model systems.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 14: practical definition is quoted.

required_facts.fact: Roles were 95.6 percent production-focused, nearly 50 percent backend-heavy, and about 20 percent often full-stack.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 16: role-shape statistics are given.

required_facts.fact: RAG appeared in 35.9 percent of descriptions, prompt engineering in 29.1 percent, LLM integration in 25.4 percent, agents in 14.4 percent, and fine-tuning in 8.5 percent.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 25-29: GenAI skill frequencies are listed.

required_facts.fact: Python appeared in 82.5 percent of roles, while TypeScript, React, and FastAPI appeared in 23.4, 14.8, and 10.7 percent.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 35-36: programming and application-layer frequencies are given.

required_facts.fact: AWS, Docker, CI/CD, and Kubernetes were more frequent than any single GenAI framework, and no framework dominated.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 56-64: infrastructure and framework frequencies and interpretation are described.

author_attribution: Attribute the analysis and proposed definition to the authors' market study; preserve that the LLM classification and percentages describe this dataset rather than an eternal role definition.
